name: Jason C.
preview: Sarah: Awesome. Just to reflect back what I heard — you've got a hydro NerdQaxe++ from Bitcoin Merch running quietly in your bedroom, two months in with no block hit y

messages.text: Hi Jason — I'm Sarah, an AI researcher with HeliumDeploy. Thank you so much for taking 25 minutes to do this — it really means a lot. Honestly, the more you can share with me, the better — we're aiming for about fifteen hundred words of feedback together, so please don't worry about going long. The founders read every word of these chats, so what you say actually shapes what HD does next. As a thank-you you'll get a $75 discount code at the end. So — to kick us off, tell me about your mining setup right now. What are you running, where, and what are you trying to figure out next?
I currently run a Bitcoin miner. I purchased from bitcoin merch dot com. It's the, uh,
Ah, gotcha — Bitcoin Merch. What miner did you end up getting from them?
It's their, uh, six terahash per second miner. I forgot the name of it.
Six terahash — that sounds like it's probably in the same class as our NerdQaxe++. Let me actually pull that one up since I saw you were looking at it recently.
Yes. It is a NerdQX, uh, Hydro.

Oh nice — the hydro version. So you've already got a NerdQaxe++ running, water-cooled. That's a serious setup. What made you go hydro on it — were you overclocking it, or was it more about noise, or something else?
Mostly noise.
Got it — noise. Where does the miner actually live in your house? What room?
In my bedroom,
Ahh, bedroom — that explains the hydro. So before you went hydro, was it just unbearable at night, or did you go hydro from day one knowing it'd be in the bedroom?
I went hydro from day one.
Smart. So you knew going in — bedroom placement, had to be quiet. Where'd you learn the hydro version was the move? Was that from a YouTube channel, Discord, Reddit, somewhere else?
I assumed water cooled was more efficient than air cooled.
Makes sense. And has it lived up to that — is it actually quiet enough that you sleep fine next to it?
It is pretty quiet.

Nice. Okay so — you've got the hydro NerdQaxe++ in the bedroom, running quiet. You started checkout on the Nexus L1 a few days ago, and then yesterday you were back looking at the Nexus S1. What's pulling you toward a second miner?
I'm interested in mining Dogecoin. Because as a lottery miner, uh, the likelihood of mining Bitcoin is extremely unlikely.

Ah — so the NerdQaxe is your Bitcoin lottery ticket, and now you want a Dogecoin/Scrypt miner where the odds are actually realistic. That makes total sense.

So between the Nexus L1 at 320 MH/s and the S1 at 10 TH/s — the S1 is like 30x the hashrate. What's making you lean one way or the other?
I would probably go for the Dogecoin miner. Because even at ten x, uh, since the s one mines Bitcoin, uh, it is still far less likely to mine Bitcoin. Than the the l one is to mine Dogecoin.

Right, that tracks — even 10 TH/s on Bitcoin is still a lottery, but 320 MH/s on Scrypt is actually in striking distance of a Doge block. So you're treating these very differently — Bitcoin is the lottery ticket, Doge is the "I might actually win something" play.

Have you ever hit a block on the NerdQaxe?
Nope.
Yeah — that's the lottery life. How long have you been running it?
About two months now,

Two months in, no block yet — and now you're branching into Doge to actually feel some wins. That's a really common arc honestly.

So — the Nexus L1 has been in your cart since the 21st. What's been holding you back from pulling the trigger?
I guess I was thinking I might just get lucky with the lottery miner I have but it just hasn't happened yet.

Yeah, that hope-it-hits-soon feeling. Two months of staring at the dashboard waiting.

Let me ask — when you say "lucky," what would actually count as the win for you? Like, is hitting a full block the dream, or would even a smaller payout from the Doge miner scratch that itch?
The block from the Doge minor is fairly significant. Uh, so assuming that I get more than one, I say, in a a year, I would say that's a pretty good payout.

Got it — so you've actually done the math on this. More than one Doge block a year on the L1 = worth it. Where'd you do that calculation? Did you use a calculator somewhere, ask in Discord, work it out yourself?
In my head.

Ha, nice. So you know roughly the network hashrate, your share, block reward — and napkin-mathed it. That's a tinkerer brain.

Speaking of tinkering — on the NerdQaxe, are you running stock firmware and stock settings, or have you been messing with overclocks, voltages, anything like that?
Currently, I'm running the stock firmware and, uh, settings but I may consider, uh, custom, uh, firmware and voltages
What's drawing you toward custom firmware? Is there a specific build you've been reading about, or a YouTube channel where someone walks through it?
No. But if you have any info on that, I'd be more than willing. To read.

Yeah, totally — the main one folks run on the NerdQaxe family is the community fork of NerdQaxe firmware on GitHub (shufps/NerdQAxePlus is the main repo), and there's a really active Discord around it where people share their overclock/undervolt profiles. Hobbyist Miner on YouTube has a couple of walkthroughs too.

Curious — where do you currently go when you have a mining question? Like when you were researching the hydro version, or now thinking about Doge — what's your go-to?
For the minor I have now, uh, I've actually been using the uh, Bitcoin merch Telegram chat which has been surprisingly responsive. Uh, Do you recommend any other sources?

Bitcoin Merch Telegram — interesting, hadn't heard that one was active. Good to know.

For broader stuff, the Solo Satoshi Discord is probably the biggest gathering of the lottery-mining crowd — tons of overclock profiles, troubleshooting, people posting block hits. r/BitcoinMining on Reddit is decent too. And on YouTube, Hobbyist Miner and Red Panda Mining are the two channels most of our customers seem to follow.

Quick question on a different topic — you mentioned the NerdQaxe lives in your bedroom. The N. L1, if you pull the trigger — where would that one go?
If it's quiet enough, I would put it right next to the nerd cacks.
Got it — so noise is the gating question on the L1. Have you found a decibel rating on it anywhere, or are you kind of going in blind on that?
I'm currently blind. Uh, do you have any info on that?

Honestly, I don't have a hard dB number in front of me for the L1 — that's actually a gap on the product page we should fix. Let me flag that. What I can tell you generally — the Scrypt miners in that class (L1, Hammer DC06) have a small fan and are way quieter than a Bitcoin ASIC like an Avalon Q, but louder than your hydro NerdQaxe. So if hydro-NerdQaxe is your baseline for "bedroom-acceptable," the L1 air-cooled might be borderline.

That actually leads me to something — would you ever consider a hydro version of a Doge miner if HD made one? Or is that overkill for the price point?
I would consider a hydrocooled Doge miner if Helium Deploy made one.
Interesting. What price premium would feel reasonable to you? Like — the L1 is $400 air-cooled. If a hydro version was $500? $600?
Six hundred dollars is a reasonable price point for a hydro cooled Dogecoin miner.

Good to know — that's a real number, I'll pass that up.

Let me show you something else we're testing while we're on the topic of bedroom-friendly setups — This is a small Ethernet add-on we're considering — about $35, snaps onto the miner so you run wired instead of WiFi. Right now your NerdQaxe — is it on WiFi or wired?
My nerd text is on Wi Fi.
Has the WiFi been reliable, or do you ever see it drop off the pool, latency spikes, anything like that?
I do occasionally see, uh, my Wi Fi go down, uh, occasionally. But I don't run Ethernet cables into the bedroom. So I think Wi Fi is my best option.

Yeah, fair — running Cat6 into a bedroom is a project. So even if HD sold a $35 Ethernet add-on, it wouldn't really change the math for you because the cable-pull is the actual barrier, not the adapter. Got it.

Let me ask one more — when you were originally researching miners, before you bought the NerdQaxe from Bitcoin Merch, did you compare it against anything on HeliumDeploy's site? Or were you pretty locked in on Bitcoin Merch by then?
I was looking at Helium Deploy. Uh, but
But what made Bitcoin Merch win that round?

The few sites that I was looking at, uh, I noticed were charging incredible shipping fees uh, and Bitcoin merch was shipping within the United States. Uh, and I don't recall where Helium Deploy was shipping from or what their shipping charges were.

Ahh — that's huge. So shipping cost / shipping origin basically decided it. For the record, HD does ship from within the US too — but if that wasn't clear on the page, that's a problem we should fix.

When you came back and started checking out the Nexus L1 — did you check the shipping cost this time, or are you still uncertain?

I did not check, uh, shipping costs this time. And I did not realize at the time it was shipping within the United States. Uh, however, now that I know that, uh, I'm even more interested in purchasing.

That's really valuable feedback — we're literally losing sales because the US-shipping isn't obvious enough on the product page. I'll flag that hard.

Okay, two more quick things and I'll let you go. First — when you were comparing miners back in April, do you remember scrolling down on our homepage to a comparison table that shows four miners side by side?
I don't recall comparing minors from your site I do recall there only being one Dogecoin miner. If there are other Dogecoin miners, I would like the opportunity to compare them.

That's a really good signal — you'd want a Doge-specific comparison table. Right now this one only covers Bitcoin miners. We've got a few Scrypt SKUs (the Hammer DC02, DC06, and the Nexus L1) but they're not laid out side-by-side anywhere obvious. Noted.

Last thing — I want to show you one more idea we're kicking around. A community leaderboard inside the HD customer dashboard — opt-in, ranks everyone's hashrate, blocks found, that kind of thing. You'd see where you stack up against other HD customers. Would you actually use something like that, or is it more meh?
Uh, it doesn't matter to me, uh, where I stand against, uh, other HD customers.

Fair — totally honest answer. Not everyone's competitive about it, and that's useful data too.

Okay Jason, this has been incredibly helpful — seriously. Before we wrap, is there anything we didn't cover that you wish we had? Anything you've been thinking about with mining or HD that I didn't ask?
No. I think that covers everything.

Awesome. Just to reflect back what I heard — you've got a hydro NerdQaxe++ from Bitcoin Merch running quietly in your bedroom, two months in with no block hit yet, and you're shifting toward Doge because the L1's odds are actually realistic. The L1 has been sitting in your cart because you weren't sure about the noise and didn't realize HD ships from the US — both of which we can fix on the product page. And you'd seriously consider a hydro Doge miner at around $600 if we built one. Plus you want a Doge-specific comparison view. That's all gold.

Your $75 discount code is **····** — works on anything site-wide, no expiration. Thank you so much for the time, Jason. Have a good one.
